hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

informal_arrangement.description: Whether the claimant is looking after someone else's child through an informal arrangement.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions about your situation.

Let me start with: **Do you have any children you're responsible for, and if so, how many?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I'm responsible for one child - my nephew Alex. He's 11 years old and lives with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. To assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex, I need to understand your arrangement a bit better.

**What are the circumstances that led to Alex living with you? For example, is this a temporary arrangement, or are you his primary carer? And are his parents still involved in his life?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Well, his parents have had some difficulties, so Alex has been living with me for a while now. It's not really a temporary thing - I'm looking after him day-to-day, making sure he gets to school, fed, all of that. His parents are still around, but I'm the one taking care of him full-time. It's just an arrangement we've worked out as a family, nothing formal or legal about it.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for explaining that. It sounds like you're providing day-to-day care for Alex.

**A few more questions to help determine your eligibility:**

1. **Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex** - for example, either of his parents?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for him. His parents aren't getting it.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's helpful to know. I have a few more questions:

**Is your local council paying anything towards Alex's accommodation or maintenance?** For example, are you receiving any foster care payments or kinship care allowances from the council for looking after him?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, I'm not getting anything from the council. It's just a family arrangement - I'm not a registered foster carer or anything like that. I'm just looking after him myself without any financial support from the local authority.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. Just a couple more questions:

**Do you live in the UK, and does Alex live with you here in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, we both live in the UK. Alex lives here with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect, thank you. Just one final question to complete the assessment:

**Are you spending money on Alex's upkeep - things like food, clothes, school supplies, pocket money, and other day-to-day expenses?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, absolutely. I'm paying for everything - his food, clothes, school things, all his day-to-day needs. I'm the one supporting him financially.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good news! **You are eligible for Child Benefit for Alex.**

Based on the information you've provided, you meet all the eligibility criteria:

- Alex is under 16 (he's 11 years old)
- You both live in the UK
- You are responsible for Alex because he lives with you and you're paying for all his day-to-day expenses (food, clothes, school supplies, etc.)
- No one else is claiming Child Benefit for him
- The local council isn't paying anything towards his accommodation or maintenance

Even though this is an informal family arrangement and you're not Alex's parent, you can still claim Child Benefit as you're looking after him and covering his expenses.

**Next steps:** You can make a claim for Child Benefit. Only one person can claim for each child, but since no one else is claiming for Alex, you're free to apply.

**Please note:** If you or your partner have an individual income over £60,000, you may need to pay a High Income Child Benefit tax charge. You can still claim Child Benefit, but you might have to pay some or all of it back through your tax return.

Is there anything else you'd like to know about claiming Child Benefit?
